name: Billable Utilisation
note: A person-by-week utilisation heatmap whose cells colour themselves with color-mix from a --v custom property, laid out on CSS subgrid so the team trend bars sit exactly over the week columns; a :has() crosshair lights the hovered row and column, the grid is arrow-key navigable with a roving tabindex, sorting reorders rows with FLIP, and the 4/8/12-week range re-derives every KPI, mix bar and trend line from the same timesheet records. Height is --dag-util-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Project Burn & Profitability
note: A DPR-aware canvas burn-up (ResizeObserver-sized, devicePixelRatio capped at 2) that plots fee burned against earned value, the planned S-curve and the fee line, then projects a forecast-at-completion cone from the cost-performance index; a what-if slider and a pending change request re-forecast the cone and the SVG margin bridge live, the crosshair reads every series by pointer or arrow keys, and a burned-versus-complete scatter and sortable table open any project. Height is --dag-burn-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Retainer Usage
note: Retainer gauges whose arcs are conic-gradients driven by a registered @property number, so they sweep with a linear() spring when the month changes, with an inner overflow ring and a pace tick; each client's month opens a cumulative-hours chart against a working-day pace line with a crosshair, a work-type split and an entry log, and a validated log-time form feeds the same records so gauge, chart, statement, rollover and overage invoice all move together. Height is --dag-retainer-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Invoices & Overdue
note: A due-date strip plot that lays every open invoice on a timeline around today, one lane per client, sized by amount and coloured by ageing band, with a segmented ageing bar whose segments filter the plot and the table; the table's bulk bar appears purely from :has(input:checked), reminders run with progress and land on each invoice's timeline in an in-component drawer, and marking an invoice paid re-derives outstanding, overdue, DSO and the cash-in forecast. Height is --dag-invoices-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Resourcing Plan
note: An eight-week allocation plan where every person row is a subgrid of the week columns, bookings are packed into lanes and placed by grid-column, and editing a booking (days a week, shift, extend, remove) re-lays the row while the Web Animations API FLIPs each bar from where it was; arrow keys move a focused booking, tentative pipeline work toggles in and out, and per-week load cells, project coverage and the stacked capacity chart are all recomputed from the same bookings. Height is --dag-resource-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: New Business Pipeline

name: Client Health Scores
note: A tunable scoring model: six raw signals are normalised once, and the weight sliders (native ranges with accent-color, shares rounded by largest remainder so they always total 100) only re-weight them — scores, bands, sparklines and the fees-at-risk headline update every frame, the table re-ranks with a FLIP once input settles, rows reveal on a view() timeline inside their own scroller, the detail ring animates an @property number through a conic gradient, and in the portfolio map each client glides to its new height. Height is --dag-health-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.

name: Timesheet Approvals
note: A keyboard-first approvals inbox (J/K to move, A to approve, S to send back): flags are derived from the entries by rule — long days, weekend work, missing notes on billable time, a closed project, a short week — and must be accepted or sent back before Approve enables; each day's header carries its own stacked hours bar so the chart lines up with the grid for free, approved rows collapse out of the queue with the Web Animations API, Approve-all-clean runs as a visible sequence, and project rows open with a grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr transition. Height is --dag-approvals-h (680px), which can be set to 100dvh in an app.
